about: The dead-end pre-triage rules. scripts/triage_candidates.py reads this file, and so do apps that suggest the same fixes, so change a rule here and nowhere else. Each key is explained under notes.

notes.min_sessions: A dead-end search with fewer sessions than this in the period is noise.
notes.min_query_chars: A search with fewer letters and digits than this (after dropping spaces and punctuation) is noise. A search of digits only is noise too.
notes.lookalike_min_chars: Searches shorter than this (letters and digits only) are never matched to a spelling twin: short words are too easy to match by accident.
notes.long_query_chars: Searches this long or longer (letters and digits only) may be max_edits_long edits from their twin; shorter ones max_edits_short.
notes.max_edits_short: Most edits (insert, delete or change one character) between a short search and a selling search for them to count as spelling twins. Searches that are equal once spaces and punctuation are dropped always count.
notes.max_edits_long: See max_edits_short, for searches of long_query_chars or more.
notes.peers: The typical revenue per search session is the median over this many busiest top searches. Revenue at stake is a dead end's sessions times that.
notes.page_intent_words: Whole words or phrases that mean the shopper wants a page (returns, store hours, gift cards), not products. A no-results search containing one is a redirect candidate.
